text:
CHAIN
L1: Re-layout (blocks 0–2 = A,A,M; blocks 3–9 = A,M; blocks 10–11 = M) -> one net extra attention stage | quantity: params_nonembed, tok/s, peak_vram_gb | baseline: 21.24M; tok/s and peak unmeasured here | expect: +0.53M (to 21.77M, +2.5%); step time +2–5%; peak VRAM +0.05–0.15 GB without checkpointing | breaks if: step time rises more than 10% or peak goes above 5.6 GB
L2: Attention in blocks 10–11 is redundant, so removing it costs about nothing | quantity: loss rise when the attention branches of blocks 10–11 are zeroed on a trained baseline checkpoint; secondarily, attention entropy in layers 10–11 | baseline: entropy 0.711 / 0.763 (ranked 8th and 7th of 12, not highest); ablation unmeasured | expect: ablation rise below 0.02 nats | breaks if: ablation rise is 0.03 nats or more, or recall-token loss rises by more than 0.05
L3: A second attention stage in blocks 0–2 adds useful early mixing (two-hop composition such as previous-token followed by copy, before any MLP) | quantity: recall-token loss, and the position gap (256–1024 minus 0–64) | baseline: recall 4.475 vs 6.704 for the rest; gap +0.459 | expect: recall loss down 0.02–0.10 at matched steps; gap shrinks | breaks if: recall loss and the gap are unchanged (within ±0.02) at step 200
L4: The new early stages actually learn | quantity: grad norm of each added attention stage | baseline: layer 0 attention 0.24 (an anomaly at z 7), layers 1–5 0.020–0.024 | expect: added stages at or above 0.02 | breaks if: added-stage grad norm is below 0.01 by step 100, meaning the stage is dead weight
L5: Net effect on exam loss | quantity: exam val_loss after 1525 steps | baseline: pooled baseline mean (not given here) | expect: −0.000 to −0.015 nats | breaks if: the difference is within ±0.005, or step-45 train loss is more than 0.03 above baseline
WEAKEST: L2

QUESTIONS
Q1: Does the measured entropy profile support the premise that deep attention is near-uniform? | decides: run the idea's own entropy gate vs replace it with an ablation gate
A1: No. Entropy is highest at layer 0 (0.957), then layers 1 (0.903) and 2 (0.854). Layers 10 and 11 are 0.711 and 0.763, ranked 8th and 7th. By the idea's own rule ("if the last two blocks are not the highest-entropy layers, drop the idea"), the 100-step data already says drop it. The rationale is inverted: extra attention would go into the *most* uniform layers. The layout may still be right for other reasons (sandwich ordering, below), so the gate should be a zero-ablation of deep attention on a trained baseline checkpoint, scored on train-shard windows, not entropy.

Q2: Is there prior evidence for "more attention at the bottom, more FFN at the top" that does not depend on the entropy argument? | decides: keep the 13/12 non-neutral layout vs a parameter-neutral 12/12 reorder as the primary build
A2: Yes. Press, Smith and Levy's sandwich transformer put extra attention sublayers at the bottom and extra FFN sublayers at the top, with the same sublayer count. It improved WikiText-103 and enwik8 language modelling, but the gain did not transfer to translation (https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.03864; recalled, not fetched this session). PAR Transformer similarly kept quality with fewer attention layers, placed mostly early (https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.04534; recalled). The idea's +0.53M params is a confound, so a parameter-neutral reorder is the needed control.

Q3: In blocks 0–2, should the stage order be A-A-M or A-M-A? | decides: A-A-M vs A-M-A
A3: A-A-M follows the sandwich pattern and lets the second attention read the first one's output before any MLP. A-M-A interleaves, which gives A,M,A,A,M,A,A,M,A,A,M… and just shifts where the doubled attention falls. Build A-A-M; it is the faithful reading of "a second attention stage".

Q4: How should per-stage stream logits be shaped so the optimizer routing does not change silently? | decides: per-block (S,4) / (S,4,4) tensors vs per-stage 1-D parameters
A4: In the script, `read_logits` and `write_logits` have shape (2,4), so the `p.ndim == 2` rule sends them to **Muon**. `mix_logits` (2,4,4) is 3-D and goes to AdamW. If the builder splits them per stage into 1-D (4,) tensors, they silently move to AdamW at lr 3e-3. Keep shapes (S,4), (S,4,4) with S = number of stages in the block. Note that MLP-only blocks then have (1,4) rows, and Muon normalises them to a unit row; that is still Muon and acceptable, but it should be noted.

Q5: Is checkpointing block 0 needed? | decides: torch.utils.checkpoint on block 0 vs no checkpointing
A5: Probably not. Activations for one attention stage including the four-stream tensors (each (4,1024,4,384) bf16 = 12.6 MB) come to roughly 80–120 MB, and the net change is +1 stage, about +0.1 GB. Baseline peak is unmeasured here, but "micro_batch 8 spilled past 6 GB" suggests micro_batch 4 sits around 3–3.5 GB. Build without checkpointing, read peak_vram_gb from `--smoke-steps 20`, and add checkpointing only if peak goes above 5.3 GB. Checkpointing also recomputes the Sinkhorn loops and adds code surface under the tripwire.

Q6: Do the deep attention stages carry copying/recall work that MLP-only blocks cannot do? | decides: drop attention in both blocks 10 and 11 vs only block 11
A6: Unknown at 21M / 50M tokens. At large scale, deep attention layers are the most removable by input/output similarity (He et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.15786; recalled). Here the recall gap is 2.23 nats and nothing shows which layers produce it. The zero-ablation of block 10 and block 11 attention, separately, on a trained baseline decides this.

Q7: Can the step-45 kill threshold (+0.03) be resolved? | decides: a single-seed step-45 comparison vs a 3-seed mean over steps 40–50
A7: Total steps = 50e6 // 32768 = 1525, and warmup = 30 steps, so step 45 is just past warmup. Loss falls about 0.019 per step there (7.062 at step 26, 6.590 at step 51), so a one-step lag reads as +0.02. Per-batch noise is unmeasured. Use the mean loss over steps 40–50, averaged over the same seeds for both arms.

Q8: Is a −0.01 gain detectable under C7 with 3 seeds? | decides: 3 seeds vs 5+ seeds per arm
A8: Likely not. With n=3 per arm (Welch df ≈ 4, one-sided t₀.₀₁ ≈ 3.75), beating the baseline by 0.005 plus a margin requires a seed std below about 0.0016 for a true effect of 0.01. Seed std at 50M tokens is unmeasured. Plan 5 seeds (t ≈ 2.9, which needs std below about 0.0027).

Q9: How will the exam reconstruct the layout? | decides: a new Config field vs a layout derived in code from n_layer
A9: The exam calls GPT(cfg) built from the saved config. Whether it uses the candidate's Config class is unknown. Derive the layout in code (or read it with `getattr(cfg, "layout", DEFAULT)`) so an exam-side Config without the field still builds the same model. A string field with a default also works through the auto-generated argparse.

Q10: What write-stream init should the third stage get? | decides: write to stream 2 vs reuse stream 0's pattern
A10: It barely matters. 2·sigmoid(0.03) = 1.015 vs 2·sigmoid(−0.01) = 0.995, and mixing starts near identity (off-diagonal about 0.0025 after Sinkhorn on exp(6) diagonals). The streams stay nearly identical early on. Use stream s mod 4 for consistency.

KNOWN
- Attention stage params: wq 221,184 + compress 49,152 + latent_norm 128 + expand 98,304 + rotary 12,288 + q/k norms 128 + wo 147,456 = 528,640; with the pre-norm and logits, 529,048 per stage [script]
- Net change is +529,048 params, giving non-embedding 21.77M (+2.5%), well under the C3 cap of 23.36M. The idea's "+0.59M" is wrong [script]
- Forward FLOPs per token: attention stage ≈ 2.0M (1.06M projections + about 0.98M causal scores), MLP ≈ 2.48M, tied head ≈ 38.6M; baseline total ≈ 93M, so +1 attention stage ≈ +2.2% FLOPs [script]
- Each stage runs a 20-iteration Sinkhorn on a 4×4 matrix, about 40 tiny kernels forward plus backward; at this size launch overhead scales with stage count (24 to 25) [script]
- read/write logits (2-D) are optimised by Muon, mix_logits (3-D) by AdamW; changing their rank changes the optimizer [script]
- The scaled-init loop touches `b.attn.wo` and `b.mlp.w_down`; with a list of attentions and attention-free blocks, the loop must iterate every attention module and tolerate none [script]
- Scaled init uses sqrt(2·n_layer)=sqrt(24); with 25 stages the difference is 2%, so keep it [script]
- total_steps = 1525, warmup 30 steps, cooldown starts at step 1067 [script]
- Attention entropy by layer at step 100: [0.957, 0.903, 0.854, 0.804, 0.771, 0.78, 0.698, 0.704, 0.705, 0.667, 0.711, 0.763]; layers 10–11 are not the most uniform [measured]
- Attention grad norms are lowest at layers 1–5 (0.020–0.024), not at the top (10: 0.0295, 11: 0.0288); layer 0 attention grad is an outlier at 0.24–0.29 [measured]
- Residual RMS grows ×7.8 across depth (1.40 to 10.89); an MLP-only top does not address this [measured]
- First-token attention mass is about 0.003 everywhere: no attention sinks yet at step 100 [measured]
- Sandwich ordering (attention-heavy bottom, FFN-heavy top, same sublayer count) helped LM perplexity but not translation: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.03864 [web, recalled]
- Deep attention layers in large LLMs are highly removable by similarity criteria: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.15786 [web, recalled]
- Entropy at step 100 reflects a model at loss 6.18, mostly using unigram/bigram statistics; the end-of-training profile may differ [belief]

ASSUMES
- Normalised attention entropy measures redundancy (but uniform attention can be useful bag-of-context averaging).
- The step-100/200 entropy profile predicts the profile after 1525 steps.
- Early blocks are attention-starved rather than MLP-starved.
- Large-model findings on deep-attention redundancy transfer to a 12-block, 21M model.
- Any gain comes from placement, not from the +0.53M extra parameters (there is no parameter-neutral control).
- Layout is a hard, whole-stage, fixed-for-all-training decision.
- The four-stream mixing absorbs a third stage with copied init without retuning.

NEW IDEAS

SLOT: drop
IDEA: Parameter-neutral sandwich reorder
MECHANISM: Drops the assumption that attention count must change. Keep 12 attention + 12 MLP stages but order them A,A,A,M | (A,M)×9 | M,M,M across 12 blocks, i.e. stage counts per block (A,A) (A,M)… (M,M). This isolates placement from parameter count.
PREDICTION: Same params and FLOPs as baseline; loss within −0.01 to +0.005.
TEST: 200-step, 3-seed matched comparison against baseline and against the 13/12 idea; if the 13/12 version wins only by the param delta, placement is not the cause.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.03864
PART: State across depth: layer count and block layout
KIND: port

SLOT: strengthen
IDEA: Ablation-placed attention budget
MECHANISM: Train one baseline to completion, zero each attention branch in turn and measure the loss rise on train-shard windows. Remove the two least important attention stages wherever they sit, and duplicate attention in the two most important blocks.
PREDICTION: The removed stages cost under 0.01 nats each in ablation; the final loss beats the fixed 0–2 / 10–11 layout.
TEST: The ablation sweep itself (12 evaluations on one checkpoint). If no stage costs under 0.02, there is nothing to move.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.15786
PART: State across depth: layer count and block layout
KIND: port

SLOT: specialise
IDEA: MLP-only final block, width reinvested
MECHANISM: Drop attention only in block 11 and spend its 528,640 params on that block's MLP (d_ff 1077 to about 1536). Nothing is added at the bottom.
PREDICTION: Parameter-neutral; loss change within ±0.005 if top attention is redundant; recall-token loss unchanged.
TEST: 200 steps on 3 seeds; recall-token loss rising more than 0.05 refutes it.
SOURCE: own
PART: State across depth: layer count and block layout
KIND: leap
BREAKS: Every block has an attention stage.
KILL: Mean train loss over steps 40–50 more than 0.03 above baseline.

SLOT: port
IDEA: Depth-tapered latent KV size
MECHANISM: Instead of moving whole stages, move attention capacity inside MLA: latent 192 / rotary 48 in blocks 0–3, 128 in blocks 4–7, 64 / 16 in blocks 8–11, with total attention params held near baseline.
PREDICTION: Same params; recall loss down 0.02–0.05 if early attention is the bottleneck.
TEST: 200 steps on 3 seeds, measuring recall-token loss and the position gap.
SOURCE: own
PART: Attention: latent KV compression and rotary split
KIND: port

SLOT: combine
IDEA: Learned layout via sparsified stage gates
MECHANISM: Combine with GateSkip-style gates. Every block gets A,A,M with a scalar sigmoid gate per attention branch (init 0.9), trained with a small L1 penalty on the gates, so training decides where attention lives. The two lowest gates' stages are pruned at step 1067 (cooldown start) to restore the parameter budget for the exam.
PREDICTION: Gates close preferentially in some band of depth; pruning at cooldown start costs under 0.005 by the end.
TEST: 300-step run printing gate values; if all gates stay above 0.7, there is no redundancy to exploit.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.13876v3
PART: State across depth: layer count and block layout
KIND: leap
BREAKS: The layout is fixed before training and identical for its whole duration.
KILL: Mean train loss over steps 40–50 more than 0.03 above baseline, or peak VRAM above 5.6 GB with 36 stages.

OPEN
- Does the per-layer entropy ordering at step 1525 match step 100 (early layers flattest)? | build: yes | decides: entropy gate vs ablation gate
- What is the zero-ablation loss cost of attention in blocks 10 and 11 on a trained baseline? | build: yes | decides: drop both vs drop only block 11
- How large is the exam val_loss seed std at 50M tokens? | build: yes | decides: 3 seeds vs 5+ seeds
- What is the baseline peak VRAM at micro_batch 4? | build: yes | decides: checkpointing block 0 vs none
- Does the exam build Config from the candidate's class or its own? | build: yes | decides: Config field vs layout derived in code
- Is any gain from placement or from +0.53M params? | build: yes | decides: 13/12 layout vs param-neutral 12/12 sandwich
- Does Muon on (1,4) / (3,4) logit matrices behave like on (2,4)? | build: no | decides: keep Muon routing vs move logits to AdamW
